title: Review of flshell2 (IBMED) on fresh seeds 7-8: shelled gliders, division and motion replicate, and the starve-one-daughter fork passes cleanly on 1 of 2 seeds; the shell is a kernel readout of the body that speeds gliders by 19-29%, so B is by construction
summary: labkit re-run of world.py on seeds 7 and 8 (rerun/, t=800) and the h5=0 twin on the same seeds (h5_0/). Every glider carries a closed S ring at 9 px (shellprof.json: S peak 0.39 vs 0.06 inside and 0.02 outside on seed 8, median closure 24/24 sectors, 60% fully closed; rerun/seed8/tracks.png). Rings fuse into shared rims when bodies meet. Persistent splits 3 and 10, max generation 2 and 7, merge/split 0.77 and 0.84 (reticulate). Top tracks travel up to 15.5 and 10.7 body lengths. With the shell feedback the top tracks' median speed is 0.575/0.517 vs 0.484/0.400 at h5=0 (+19%/+29%), but moving tracks (27/41 vs 46/26), max body lengths (15.5/10.7 vs 12.9/12.4) and splits (3/10 vs 9/7) are mixed. Starve-one-daughter fork (the author's dfork.py, 300 t). Seed 8: the followed daughter falls 61 -> 0 by t=349 while its sister persists (77) and the same daughter in the fed twin grows to 87. Seed 7: the chosen pair re-merged at t~200 in both arms, so the fork is confounded; under the cut the merged body shrinks steadily 133 -> 28 (21%) by t=470, while in the fed twin it holds 100-210 (fork/fork78.png). S is grown where a ring convolution of the body hits a set point and has no transport. It is a band-pass readout of the body with memory; it contains nothing, and its only work is a modest speed-up.

observations.I: rerun/seed8/tracks.png: discrete gliders, each in its own ring, persisting between divisions and merges
observations.M: speedcmp.json: top tracks travel up to 15.5 (seed 7) and 10.7 (seed 8) body lengths with body and ring intact (rerun/seed8/tracks.png #86, #83)
observations.E: fork/fork78.png seed 8: food cut following one daughter from t=155, it falls 61 -> 0 by t=349 while its sister keeps 77 and the same daughter in the fed twin grows to 87
observations.D: rerun/SUMMARY.md: persistent splits 3 (gen 2) and 10 (gen 7), merge/split 0.77 and 0.84

seeds_run.result: pass (I, M, D; fork confounded: the pair re-merged)

controls_run.E: fork/df8.log, fork/df7.log (dfork.py seeds 7 and 8, 300 t, fed twin vs food cut following one daughter); seed 8 clean pass, seed 7 confounded by a re-merge
controls_run.B: h5_0/seed7, seed8 (shell feedback off): top-track median speed 0.484/0.400 vs 0.575/0.517 with it; other motion and split measures mixed

verdicts.limitation: B: S is produced wherever a ring-kernel convolution of the body density hits a set point, has no transport, and holds nothing. Per RUBRIC L3 it is a readout of the body field (a contour by construction), and its demonstrated work is a 19-29% speed-up of the top tracks with other motion measures mixed, so I put B under by_construction. E: one clean fork in two; on seed 7 the forked pair re-merged, and the merged body starved to 21% without crossing the 10% line within 300 t. Build-from-food matter makes the dependence by construction apart from the fork. D is reticulate (merges ~0.8 of splits). Planted noise patch, so S does not apply.
